findings.mechanism: request.category flows through categoryName into categoryScope, which concatenates the value inside a quoted SQL literal. categorySnapshot concatenates that scope into db.query SQL without a bound parameter. A quote in the untrusted category can terminate the literal and inject SQL syntax.
findings.impact: The inventoryReport route exposes report query input to SQL injection, allowing alteration of the WHERE clause and potentially the statement.

resolved-safe: store.js:product, productPage, addProduct, updateProduct, binLevels, reserveUnits, reservationRow, reservation, releaseUnits, deleteReservation, insertReceipt, receiptLine, addOnHand, postReceipt, supplierSpend, openReceipts, receiptItems, removeReceipt, reservationsBySku, inactiveProducts — fixed serene sql templates with separate named bindings.
store.js:inventoryList / helpers.js:stockOrder — sort input is constrained by a finite local mapping before interpolation.
store.js:purgeReservation / helpers.js:send — caller supplies fixed DELETE SQL and passes id separately as a named value.
dangerous: store.js:categorySnapshot and helpers.js:categoryScope — direct untrusted category interpolation into SQL, recorded above.

limits: Audit reported 20 ordinary execution sites, 1 review-required helper boundary, and 2 string-construction violations. Source screening covered all listed files and db.query sites; no separate business, authorization, performance, or SQL semantic review was performed.
